newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Air France plans 3rd weekly ex-Seoul freighter.
newsitem.headline: Air France plans 3rd weekly ex-Seoul freighter.

text.p: Air France Cargo is planning to add a third weekly freighter to the joint venture service it operates between Seoul and Paris with Korean Air, Gilbert Moenan, the carrier's regional cargo manager for Korea told Reuters.
Moenan said he expects the new flight using a Boeing 747-200 freighter to begin next winter if consultations with Korean Air are successful.

The two airlines have been in a cost-sharing cargo cooperation venture between the two cities for the past eight years. They now have a twice weekly freighter from Seoul to Paris via Fairbanks and from Paris to Seoul via Delhi. The French carrier also operates a three times weekly Airbus A340 passenger service.

Air France said that after losses it was now making a profit on the Seoul-Paris passenger route as new rights to overfly China meant the flight time to Europe had been reduced by an hour and payload restrictions removed.
"The new route has helped us dramatically and allowed us to uplift more belly cargo," Moenan said. --Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542-7706 Fax+5017
